newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Bougainville not a lost cause.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Bougainville not a lost cause.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Sunday that it did not regard the Bougainville copper mine at the centre of the political turmoil in Papua New Guinea as a lost cause.

"No, it's not - it's still a very, very important asset ... and we still would like to go back there," said RTZ-CRA chief executive Leon Davis when asked by a television interviewer if Bougainville was a lost cause.
Secessionist rebels on Bougainville Island closed the Panguna copper mine operated by RTZ-CRA's 53.6 percent owned Bougainville Copper Ltd in May 1989.
"We've been saying for the last eight years that for Bougainville (mine) to be viable, we have to have a political settlement in Bougainville, not a military one," Davis said.
He said he had had no word from the PNG government on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan's comment that he wanted to see the RTZ-CRA stake in Bougainville Copper bought out.
"We haven't heard anything official - all we know about buying out Bougainville Copper is what we read in the paper," he said.
He said Papua New Guinea remained conducive to foreign investment.

"The laws of the country are still conducive to foreign investment but what is happening in Bougainville - between Bougainville and the central government of PNG - is of obvious concern to us," Davis said.
RTZ-CRA's assets in the country also include a 17 percent stake in the big Lihir gold mine, scheduled to start production before end-1997.
